lesson.meaning: To look at two or more things to see how they are similar or different.
examples: Before buying a new phone, I always compare the features and prices of different models.
Let's compare the sales figures from this quarter with last quarter's to see our growth.
The manager asked us to compare the two project proposals and recommend the best one.
It's not fair to compare your progress with someone else's; everyone learns at their own pace.
Can you compare the benefits of working from home versus working in the office?
lesson.memory_tip: Mama's Tip: Remember, when you 'compare', you're checking what's the SAME and what's DIFFERENT, just like comparing two apples to see which is bigger or sweeter!
